How these numbers are worked out
How these numbers are worked out
"Full speed" is what the buildings would do if they never stopped. It comes straight from their recipe.
"Right now" comes from the game's timers. It records how long each machine works, applies that share to its recipe, and averages over 12 months.
Rainwater harvesters have no timer either. Their figure is the game's own formula, around 42 rainy days a year on a normal map, spread over 12 months. A drought or a storm will give something else.
Farms and product-burning generators keep no timers either. Only their capacity is shown, and the warnings above name the ones in your selection.
Electricity weighs what the buildings draw at full speed against what the local generators could put out. Solar panels count at their peak, reached only in full sun.
